==Problem 11==

The ratio of the length to the width of a rectangle is <math>4</math> : <math>3</math>. If the rectangle has diagonal of length <math>d</math>, then the area may be expressed as <math>kd^2</math> for some constant <math>k</math>. What is <math>k</math>?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ \frac{2}{7}\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ \frac{3}{7}\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ \frac{12}{25}\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ \frac{16}{25}\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ \frac{3}{4}</math>

==Solution 1==
Let the rectangle have length <imath>4x</imath> and width <imath>3x</imath>. Then by <imath>3-4-5</imath> triangles (or the Pythagorean Theorem), we have <imath>d = 5x</imath>, and so <imath>x = \dfrac{d}{5}</imath>. Hence, the area of the rectangle is <imath>3x \cdot 4x = 12x^2 = \dfrac{12d^2}{25}</imath>, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\;\frac{12}{25}}</imath>

==Solution 2==

Let the side lengths of the rectangle be <imath>3</imath> and <imath>4</imath>. Therefore, the diagonal of the rectangle is <imath>5</imath>. The area of the rectangle would be <imath>3\cdot{4}=12.</imath> Thus, <imath>25k=12</imath>, so <imath>k=\boxed{\text{(C)} \frac{12}{25}}.</imath>
